source: Gallica IIIF, BnF Melanges de Colbert 155 (828 canvases; manifest carries no folio labels at all -- every canvas labelled 'NP', confirmed by tools/gallica_folio.py --list on the cached manifest, sources/gallica-manifests/btv1b100340323.json)
canvas_rule: One canvas per page side (recto/verso), not per leaf/opening: canvas 207 carries the pencil foliation '133' top-right and canvas 209 carries '134' top-right, both read by eye; canvas 208 (between them, no foliation visible in the 800px probe crop) is folio 133 verso by this run of three. Not confirmed at any other point in the volume -- a future worker relying on this offset elsewhere should re-anchor by eye first (tools/gallica_folio.py --anchor).

date_bisection.read: Cover leaf, printed label 'COLB. 155 MEL.'; no date.

A memoire (not a dated letter) about a privilege for a glass/mill works in Florence, quoting internal dates '20e janvier 1669', '20e juin 1670', and '20e aoust et 12e septembre 1670' -- places this document's own date shortly after 12 Sept 1670, i.e. after the target's 13 Aug 1670, confirming the target lies before canvas 414. Canvas index does not track calendar date linearly across the volume (memoires and letters vary greatly in length), so this was read directionally only, not used for linear interpolation.
Folded letter address panel to 'M. le duc de Montausier', datestamp 'decembre 1670' -- confirms the volume's last canvas is in December 1670.

TARGET FOUND on this single bisection probe (midpoint of [2,414]): cipher numeral groups (top ~9 lines) followed by a clear-text closing -- 'Monsieur, vostre tres humble et tres obeissant serviteur, P. de Bonzy E. de Béziers', dateline 'A Madrid le 13 aoust 1670', and a sideways marginal filing note reading '[M. l']Evesque de Bézie[rs] 13 aoust 1670'. Exact match to NOTES.md's target (Bishop of Beziers, Madrid, 13 August 1670).

207.content: Clear-text French narrative continuing from an earlier folio (colonial affairs: the Indies, a French corsair scare, the Honduras post, the Council of the Indies), running to the bottom of the page where it switches into cipher numeral groups -- the first line of which is the letter's opening cipher (see eye_check below).

208.content: Continues the cipher numeral groups for about 9 lines, then closes in clear: courtesy close, signature 'P. de Bonzy E. de Béziers' (Pierre de Bonzy, Bishop of Beziers), dateline 'A Madrid le 13 aoust 1670', and a sideways marginal filing annotation naming the same. This is the letter's last leaf: canvas 209/folio 134r begins a different, unrelated letter (see below).

206.content: Clear-text French, same colonial-affairs narrative as folio 133r's top (continuous prose across the page break) -- confirms the letter runs to at least this folio backward; its true opening folio (with the letter's salutation) was not located within this job's network cap and is a named next step.

209.content: A DIFFERENT, unrelated letter starts here: dateline 'Charles ce 23 aoust' (a different date and, given the place name, a different correspondent), salutation 'Monsieur, j'ay trop de reconnoissance...', entirely in clear text. Confirms canvas 208/folio 133v is the Beziers letter's own last leaf, not a shared page with what follows.

eye_check.method: Read the first line of cipher numerals at the bottom of canvas 207 (folio 133r) by eye, looked up each sign in keys/key_colbert_croissy_1668.tsv (sign, diacritic) -> value, and compared the assembled plaintext to known_plaintext.txt's printed crib.
eye_check.decode: 2=a, 62=fi, 14=n -> 'afin'; 107=que -> 'que'; 27m=si, 91m=le, 14=n, 20=t -> 'silent'; 21m=re, 16=p, 22m=ri, 28m=se -> 'reprise'. Assembled: 'afin que silent reprise', an exact match to known_plaintext.txt (Tomokiyo's printed three-word-plus opening, quoted with a trailing ellipsis). The remaining signs on the line (213, 15, 12, 20) are beyond the printed crib and not decoded here (213 has no row in the key at any diacritic tried -- left for the calibrated reader named in NOTES.md's next step, not solved by this job).
eye_check.grade: S (cryptanalytic result via a printed key against a printed crib, not a full reading) -- confirms the folio, does not constitute a decode of the letter.
